page: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9R05 processors operating at clock speeds up to 5.0 GHz, the instance delivers 24 physical x86_64 cores across 24 dedicated vCPUs with a single thread per core execution model. The CPU subsystem incorporates 48 KB L1 data cache, 1 MB L2 cache, 32 MB L3 cache, and robust vector extension support including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16 for accelerated numerical computation.

System memory is configured with 768.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 RAM clocked at 6 GHz, yielding a high memory-to-core allocation of 32.0 GB per physical core. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier large-block uncached memory throughput, achieving 393.14 GB/sec for reads and 208.57 GB/sec for writes. Single-core and multi-core computational metrics place the instance in the upper decile, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 3,116 and a multi-core score of 28,417, as well as stress-ng compute tests scoring in the top 10% for single-threaded tasks.

Storage and networking subsystems include 1,900 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network throughput of 19 Gbps. The local NVMe disk provides high IOPS and low-latency scratch space without incurring network storage overhead, while the network tier supports sustained throughput across distributed architectures. The server contains no integrated GPUs, relying entirely on the host CPU for execution routines.

From an efficiency perspective, the platform consolidates massive DDR5 memory density with dedicated high-clock AMD EPYC compute and local NVMe storage into a single node. This reduces the requirement to scale across multiple instances for RAM-bound tasks, though the resource mix introduces cost inefficiencies if the heavy memory pool or high single-thread clock speeds remain underutilized. The instance is suited for in-memory databases like Redis, massive caching tiers, real-time analytics, large in-memory graph processing, CPU-based transformer inference, and enterprise database workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services x8aedz.6xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 24 dedicated physical x86_64 cores from an AMD EPYC 9R05 processor running up to 5.0 GHz. Designed for memory-intensive computations, it pairs 768.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM (32.0 GB per core) with 1,900 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and 19 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Top-tier benchmark results highlight uncached memory read bandwidth of 393.14 GB/sec, write bandwidth of 208.57 GB/sec, and a Geekbench multi-core score of 28,417. CPU instruction support includes AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI, which deliver high-throughput CPU-based model inference alongside 94.63 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking dedicated GPU accelerators, its substantial DDR5 footprint and direct NVMe storage offer high density for in-memory key-value stores, large operational databases, and memory-bound analytics pipelines.
